cards.text: Jesus has just asked the Pharisees a question they can't answer, and from that day on nobody dares question Him anymore (Matthew 22:46). Now He turns to the crowds and His disciples and talks about the scribes and Pharisees, the teachers of the law and the religious leaders. He starts by saying they sit in Moses' seat.

cards.question: Since the scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, Jesus tells the crowds to ignore everything they teach.

cards.text: So practice what they tell you, BUT here comes the catch, friend. Follow the recipe card, just don't copy the baker.

cards.question: Why does Jesus tell the crowds not to do what the scribes and Pharisees do?

answers.text: They do not practice what they preach
They copy the customs of foreigners
They change the law every single year

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: they tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on people's shoulders.

cards.question: The scribes and Pharisees lay heavy loads on people's shoulders. How much do they help move them?

answers.text: They will not lift a finger
They carry half of the load
They help only on feast days

cards.text: That's the friend who signs you up to help him move, then spends all Saturday on the couch pointing at boxes and saying, "Careful, that one's HEAVY."

cards.question: Jesus says all the deeds of the scribes and Pharisees are done for ___ to see.

cards.text: They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels. Friend, if a taller chef's hat got me noticed, I'd have stretched mine till it scraped the ceiling, and I am NOT proud of that.
Then Jesus starts listing what they love, and friend, this is not a short list. This is a "scroll down, there's more" list.

cards.question: At banquets, the scribes and Pharisees love the places of ___.
Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.

cards.text: And they love being addressed by the title Rabbi. That's the guy who makes assistant shift lead and has his email signature updated before lunch.

cards.question: Jesus says His listeners are not to be called Rabbi. Why not?

answers.text: They have one Teacher and are all brothers
The title belongs only to the priests
They have not studied long enough yet

cards.question: Jesus says not to call anyone on earth your ___, because you have one in heaven.
Jesus tells His listeners not to be called instructors, because their one Instructor is Moses, whose seat the scribes and Pharisees sit in.

cards.text: Then Jesus says who the greatest among them shall be, and friend, I have read this line a HUNDRED times and I still gasp like it's the first time.

cards.question: According to Jesus, who shall be the greatest among His listeners?

answers.text: The one who is your servant
The one with the best seat
The one who teaches the most

cards.question: Whoever exalts himself will be ___, and whoever humbles himself will be ___.

cards.text: And that's where this batch comes out of the oven. Jesus has a whole lot more to say, so keep that apron ON, friend.

findings.problem: This story card is only a modern moving-day joke about the previous answer. It does not tell another part of the passage or move the walkthrough forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: No earlier card introduces the idea that the scribes and Pharisees do their deeds to be seen by other people. Choosing "men" rather than "God" or "angels" therefore depends on guessing unseen wording rather than reasoning out the meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never identifies the one Instructor as "the Christ." Correctly marking this statement False only rejects Moses, so the key identification in verse 10 remains untold.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
